overal.goal: `startServer` always started a WebhookDispatcher, so two `serve` processes on one data root (for example a second serve next to a runner-owning one, or a `--no-runner` one) both read the event feed and POSTed every event: double delivery, and they overwrote each other's cursors and retry state in webhooks/state.json. Run the dispatcher only in the server that holds a pid lock on <data>/webhooks/.dispatcher.lock; a second server retries periodically and takes over when the holder exits or dies. Not tied to the runner guard, because a lone --no-runner serve must still deliver. Found in the review of runner-guard-identity (2026-11-02).

versions.version: Filed from the runner-guard-identity review (I2, 2026-11-02); not started.

runDispatcherWhileHolding (packages/web/src/webhooks.ts) starts the dispatcher only while the process holds webhooks/.dispatcher.lock and retries the lock every 5 s (webhookLockRetryMs); startServer uses it and stop() releases it. Tests: in-process gates (one holder at a time, takeover on stop, stop before or during the first attempt), and two real servers (startServer in tsx children, webhooks-process.test.ts) with one receiver: 8 events delivered once each, the holder SIGKILLed after the first 5 and the other server delivers the last 3. Without the gate the same test sees every event twice.

tests.strategy: Child-process servers on one scratch data root and an HTTP receiver in the test.
